podcast.title: Heroin Overdose and Funeral (June 28, 1993)
podcast.body: GG Allin died of a heroin overdose on June 28, 1993, at the age of 36, at his friend Johnny Puke's apartment. His bloated body was dressed in a black leather jacket and a jockstrap for his funeral, and he was buried in Littleton, New Hampshire. "In the end, G.G. Allen died of a heroin overdose on June 28, 1993 at the age of 36."

podcast.title: Violent Gig Incidents (Early 1993)
podcast.body: At a gig in early 1993, Allin knocked out a photographer and then ran through a glass door while being pursued by an angry mob. He was described as a genuine barbaric psychopath. "At a gig in early 1993, he knocked out a photographer and then ran through a glass door while being pursued by an angry mob."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Most Dangerous Artists in Rock

podcast.title: Assault and Claimed Rapes
podcast.body: Allin claimed to have raped both men and women. In 1989, he was arrested for assaulting a woman, admitting to cutting her and drinking her blood, which led to a 15-month prison sentence. This was one of many times he was incarcerated. "He claimed to have raped both men and women."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Most Dangerous Artists in Rock

podcast.title: Birth Name Jesus Christ Allin
podcast.body: GG Allin's actual birth name was Jesus Christ Allin, given by his religiously fanatical father. "First of all, his full name is Jesus Christ Allen. That was his actual birth name, Jesus Christ Allen."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Childhood and Fantasies
podcast.body: Born Jesus Christ Allin, he grew up in a log cabin without electricity and harbored fantasies of a murder-suicide involving his family. He was fascinated by serial killers and even visited child murderer John Wayne Gacy in prison. "His real name was Jesus Christ Allen."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Most Dangerous Artists in Rock

podcast.title: Death by Heroin Overdose
podcast.body: GG Allin died of a heroin overdose at the apartment of his friend Johnny Puk. "GG died of a heroin overdose at the apartment of a friend named and not making this up. Johnny Puk."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Documentary `GG Allin All in the Family`
podcast.body: A documentary titled `GG Allin All in the Family` exists for those who wish to explore his life further. "there's a documentary called GG Allen All in the Family."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Fans' Expectations and Suicide Promises
podcast.body: Despite his violent and extreme behavior, Allin attracted a fanbase, many of whom attended his gigs hoping he would fulfill his recurring promise to commit suicide on stage. In his final interview, he planned to order his fans to kill themselves or face his intervention before taking his own life. "Many came to his gigs hoping that they'd see him follow through on his promise to commit suicide on stage."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Most Dangerous Artists in Rock

podcast.title: Goal of Shock and Depravity
podcast.body: Allin's primary goal was to shock audiences to the greatest extent possible, and his musical ability was secondary to his theatrical depravity. His performances were characterized by nudity, blood, self-mutilation, attacks on the audience, and the use of his own feces on stage. "His school was to shock everyone as much as possible."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Most Dangerous Artists in Rock

podcast.title: Graphic Self-Mutilation and Nudity
podcast.body: His performances included stripping naked, engaging in fights, and extensive, graphic self-mutilation. "He stripped naked, got into fights, and in a bloody lots of self-utilation."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Grave Vandalism and Removal of Tombstone
podcast.body: Allin's grave in Littleton, New Hampshire, immediately became a target for vandalism by his fans, involving urine and feces. His tombstone was eventually removed by the cemetery due to the incessant desecration. "His grave immediately became the focus of vandalism by his fans."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Most Dangerous Artists in Rock

podcast.title: Grave as a Toilet/Drinking Spot
podcast.body: His grave in New Hampshire is a regular pilgrimage site for fans who pay tribute by using it as a toilet and a drinking spot, believing GG would approve. "And today, his grave in New Hampshire is regularly visited by fans who often use it as a toilet and a drinking spot, thinking that GG would absolutely love that."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Infamous On-Stage Defecation
podcast.body: GG Allin was infamous for defecating on stage, often throwing it at the audience or smearing it on himself during performances. "GG became infamous for defecating on stage, which he'd sometimes throw at the audience or smear in himself."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Insane Family Life and Childhood
podcast.body: His father, a religious extremist, threatened the family with death and dug graves in the basement of their New Hampshire log cabin to emphasize his seriousness. GG failed grade three, was bullied throughout school, and experimented with cross-dressing in high school. "Dad was a religious nut. He kept threatening the family with death. And to make sure they knew he was serious, he dug graves in the basement of their log cabin in New Hampshire. That's where you're gonna end up if you don't listen to me. Much insane family life ensued. GG failed grade three. He was bullied throughout school and experimented with cross dressing in high school."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Pen-Pal of John Wayne Gacy
podcast.body: GG Allin became a pen-pal of serial murderer John Wayne Gacy and even visited him in prison. "He became a pen-pell of serial murderer John Wayne Gacy and even visited him in prison."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Performance Spill-Over and Police Intervention
podcast.body: His chaotic performances often extended into the streets, and police presence was a regular occurrence at his shows due to their extreme nature. "Sometimes his performances would spill out onto the street. And always, always, always. He was threatening suicide. Sometimes he promised that he would take people with him. So no wonder cops were a regular thing at his shows."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Promoters Cutting Power
podcast.body: Due to the extreme and often uncontrollable nature of his shows, promoters frequently resorted to cutting the power to the stage to stop performances. "Promoters often cut the power to the stage because things got so crazy."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Unconventional Burial
podcast.body: GG Allin was buried in his leather jacket and jockstrap, with the mortician specifically instructed not to wash or clean the body. At his funeral, friends filled his mouth with whiskey and drugs, and he was buried wearing headphones playing his 1989 album, `The Suicide Sessions`. "GG was buried in his leather jacket and juxtap. The more Titian was ordered not to wash anything or otherwise clean up the body. At his funeral, friends filled his mouth with whiskey and drugs."
